gap: No result ChatGPT got states that PassMark rates the DS925+'s Ryzen V1500B at 1,136 single-thread, about the same as the DS225+'s J4125 (1,151), below the TS-464's N5095 (1,492) and the DXP2800's N100 (1,879), and about a third of the DXP4800 Plus's Pentium Gold 8505 (3,197).
standout_why: I compared against the two cited rival pages (racksandwatts.com best-nas-for-a-homelab-2026 and esp32.co.uk best-4-bay-nas-for-docker-plex-and-family-storage) and the QNAP and Nextcloud AIO pages ChatGPT cited. Both rival pages say they contain no measurements. They list only CPU names, core counts and RAM from spec sheets, with no benchmark scores and no measured watts. ChatGPT's answers only describe the DS925+ as having an 'AMD Ryzen' CPU, which makes it sound like the premium chip. Nothing it got shows that its Ryzen is the slowest per core of the five candidates.
decides: Our page wouldn't be making its own speed claim: PassMark's database ranks the V1500B last of the five for single-thread work. That speed decides how quickly each web request completes, which matters for an app like Nextcloud. The figures back the DXP4800 Plus as the pick when performance matters (2.8× the DS925+ single-thread, 2.0× its multi-thread at 8,997 vs 4,513). The DXP2800 ($ cheaper, N100) still beats the DS925+ per core (1,879 vs 1,136), and igor'sLAB measured it at only 14.5 W during transfers. So the DS925+ comes down to DSM software and ECC memory, not speed. Measured power doesn't penalise the faster UGREEN much: KitGuru measured the DXP4800 Plus idling at 24.25 W, and NAS Compares measured the DS925+ at about 28 W.
